The connection between psychological stress and elevated blood glucose is not metaphorical or indirect. It is a specific, named, well-characterized molecular pathway connecting the brain’s threat detection system to the liver’s glucose production machinery through a chain of hormonal and receptor signaling events that can be traced from the amygdala to the PEPCK enzyme in the hepatocyte in four specifically named steps.

What parts of the brain are insulin sensitive? Note that the prefrontal cortex does more than help us make good decisions. It controls our behavior. Does this mean a ketogenic diet's alternative energy source to glucose would be effective? The answer is nuanced for APOE4 carriers. APOE4 carriers can take up and burn ketones, they just tend to experience a delayed or attenuated cognitive benefit compared to non-carriers. they have transport and mitochondrial bottlenecks. Plus, a ketogenic diet presents difficulties for APOE4 carriers because they are hyper-absorbers of dietary cholesterol and are significantly more prone to severe spikes in LDL cholesterol and vascular inflammation when eating a diet high in saturated fats. Because vascular health directly impacts dementia risk, many clinicians advise APOE4 carriers who want to try ketosis to rely on monounsaturated and omega-3 fats (olive oil, avocados, nuts, fatty fish) rather than butter, coconut oil, or heavy cream.
